content.title: Brazil and Mexico to play Legends match in Mexico City on 19 April
content.text: Story byBrazil and Mexico to play Legends match in Mexico City on 19 AprilIn a historic match, legends from Brazil and Mexico will face off in a festive game on Sunday, April 19, at the Azteca Stadium, in Mexico City, at 8 p.m. (Brasília time). The meeting of great football names from both countries, organized by the company Never Say Never (NSN), promises to be an unforgettable moment on the eve of the World Cup and will bring together passion, memories, and spectacle for fans at the stadium and around the world.The event is part of a series of preparations by Mexico City as one of the World Cup host cities and marks the reopening events of the legendary Azteca Stadium, now renamed Banorte Stadium.AdvertisementThe Brazilian National Team will feature renowned stars such as world champions Ronaldinho Gaúcho, Aldair, Gilberto Silva, Paulo Sérgio, Müller, Kaká, Edílson, Lúcio, Edmílson, Anderson Polga, and Juninho Paulista, as well as players who competed in World Cups and made history with the Seleção and Brazilian football, such as Adriano, Júlio César, Maicon, Giovani, Amaral, Djalminha, and Gomes.Leading the national team will be none other than three-time world champion Jairzinho, the Hurricane of the 1970 World Cup, top scorer of that tournament, and the only player to score in every match for his national team in a World Cup. The coaching staff will include major names such as fitness coach Moraci Santana, doctor José Luiz Runco, physiotherapist Luiz Rosan, and masseur Luizão.For Mexico, national stars such as Rafa Márquez, Jared Borgetti, Oswaldo Sánchez, Miguel Layún, and Andrés Guardado, all idols of local football, will take the field.The expectation is that the match will bring together fans from different generations to once again see on the pitch some of the protagonists of memorable moments in international football.AdvertisementThe match will also mark the debut of Brazil Legends, which seeks to bring back historic names and relive great achievements of Brazilian football.For the Brazilian National Team, the game will symbolize a remarkable return to Azteca Stadium, where the Seleção won its third World Cup in 1970 with one of the greatest teams in history. Led by Zagallo, stars such as King Pelé, Jairzinho, Tostão, Gérson, Clodoaldo, Rivellino, and Carlos Alberto Torres put Brazil at the top of world football.The match will be broadcast in Brazil on free-to-air television by Xsports.This article was translated into English by Artificial Intelligence. You can read the original version in 🇧🇷 here.Story byThe World Cup is coming back to North America for the first time since 1994, which means the hype machine is officially warming up and there’s no turning it off now.Over the next few months, Yahoo Sports is counting down with a daily post about the biggest sporting event on the planet: the numbers, the moments, the absurd scale of it all. Some days it’ll be history. Some days it’ll be pure spectacle. Some days it’ll be a reminder that half a billion people tuning in for a random Tuesday match is somehow normal for this sport.AdvertisementThe 2026 version of the World Cup is gearing up to be complicated, messy, political and overwhelming. But once it’s here, it’ll stop the world in a way almost nothing else can.So this is the build, one day at a time. Let’s go!June 11 - July 19 | Canada, Mexico, United StatesThis is part of our 2026 World Cup countdown. It’ll be 100 days of stories capturing the reach, history and absurd magnitude of soccer’s biggest stage. Check back daily as we build toward kickoff on June 11.Story byThe countdown to the 2026 World Cup is on! Each day ahead of the tournament’s return to North America, Yahoo Sports will highlight an insight or moment that showcases just how grand the world’s biggest sporting spectacle has become — even beyond the expanded field of this year’s global event.Eric Wynalda’s first World Cup experience ended in embarrassment after 52 minutes.AdvertisementCzechoslovakia's Ľubomír Moravčík baited the U.S. forward after continually stepping on Wynalda’s foot throughout their match in the 1990 World Cup. Wynalda, tired of the gamesmanship, shoved Moravčík, which was spotted by Kurt Röthlisberger, who brandished a red card.Four years later, Wynalda would get a second chance and redeem himself in front of 73,000 fans at the Pontiac Silverdome.That opportunity almost never came to fruition for Wynalda, who made 106 appearances for the U.S. The night before the team’s opening match of the 1994 World Cup against Switzerland, he felt a rash begin to develop on his body. He took medicine to treat it, but did not get a good night's sleep (the O.J. Simpson White Bronco chase being that same night didn’t help anyone’s ability to get plentiful rest).A switch from Powerade to Gatorade by the team caused Wynalda to break out in hives. He was so fatigued from the lack of sleep and the allergic reaction that he was subbed out in the 57th minute and left the field with swollen, red hands.AdvertisementBut just before halftime, Wynalda made his mark on the match.His 45th-minute goal would help the U.S. start the 1994 World Cup off with a 1-1 draw."It definitely was the best goal of my life," Wynalda said later. "You really have to hit that shot perfectly for it to work, and that's what happened."Wynalda wasn't even the main free-kick taker on the squad. That was Claudia Reyna's job, but an injured hamstring ruled him out for the tournament. Tab Ramos could have been the one, but he told Wynalda that the 28-yard distance was out of his range.“In that minute, it seemed to me as if there was no one else in the stadium. I just swung my foot at the ball and it flew in,” Wynalda said. “The noise that greeted me was deafening.”AdvertisementThe U.S would go on and beat Colombia and lose to Romania in its final two group stage matches. The four points were good enough to advance to the knockout round where they would fall to eventual champions Brazil, 1-0.Wynalda's goal in 1994 was one of the 34 he scored for the U.S. When he retired in 2000, he was the all-time leading scorer for the U.S. men's team. His record would stand for eight years before being passed by Landon Donovan.Story byThe countdown to the 2026 World Cup is on! Each day ahead of the tournament’s return to North America, Yahoo Sports will highlight an insight or moment that showcases just how grand the world’s biggest sporting spectacle has become — even beyond the expanded field of this year’s global event.Bob Gansler was so fearful of Trinidad & Tobago’s counterattack that he instructed midfielder Paul Caligiuri to stay back with a defensive mindset.AdvertisementCaligiuri wanted to obey his manager’s directive, but when a T&T player approached him for a tackle as he was on the ball instinct took over. Not wanting to turn the ball over and allow the opponents to go the other way for a scoring opportunity, Caligiuri feinted to his right, caught the player off-balance as he took a touch to the left.Now, Caligiuri had time and space just in front of the penalty arc. With no hesitation the California native fired a left-footed shot on the bounce with topspin.T&T goalkeeper Michael Maurice, staring into the sun at Hasely Crawford Stadium in Port of Spain, dove to his left unsuccessfully. He would later attribute his delayed reaction to being obstructed by one of his own players and not seeing the moment Caligiuri struck the ball.Caligiuri, who was playing in midfield after serving as a right back during camp, wasn’t certain his shot in the 31st minute would go in, but he knew he hit it good enough and it had a chance.The soccer version of the “shot heard 'round the world” would give the United States a 1-0 win after they hung on for the final hour of the match.AdvertisementThe match, played Nov. 19, 1989, was the final one for both teams in the CONCACAF Championship, which determined the region's qualification for the 1990 World Cup in Italy. The Soca Warriors needed only a draw to take the second and final qualifying spot. The U.S. had no other option but to win.Those three secured points booked the U.S. a spot in the Italia ‘90 field and put them into the World Cup for the first time since 1950.Caligiuri scored only five times in 110 appearances for the U.S. The Port of Spain goal was his second career international goal. His fourth came seven months later during the Americans' opening match of the 1990 World Cup, a 5-1 defeat to Czechoslovakia.The U.S. would lose all three games in Italy, but 1990 was the start of a run of seven straight World Cup appearances.AdvertisementThat streak would end, however, at the hands of T&T on Oct. 10, 2017. A win and the U.S. would’ve qualified for the 2018 World Cup. With a draw or a loss, it would have still been possible, but the Americans would have needed help to get in.The soccer gods did not shine down on the U.S. that night. Not only did they lose, but Panama and Honduras, who could have helped, both won their respective matches against Costa Rica and Mexico to drop the Americans to fifth in the group and out of contention.Powered bySpain's 2026 World Cup album drops Brazil spoilers, take a lookWith the official release in Brazil scheduled for May 1, the highly anticipated 2026 World Cup sticker album has already started being sold at some newsstands in Spain.Collectors who bought the product early noticed significant surprises on the page dedicated to the Brazilian National Team, currently coached by Carlo Ancelotti, according to Estadão.Panini’s ‘lineup’The biggest absence in this year’s edition is Neymar. For the first time after appearing in four consecutive World Cup albums, the forward did not get his own sticker.AdvertisementHis call-up for the World Cup is still considered uncertain. Panini had already left the player out of another official competition product, the Adrenalyn XL card game.On the other hand, the publication does include a sticker of Rodrygo.The detail is that the forward is certain to miss the World Cup after suffering a torn anterior cruciate ligament and meniscus in his right knee.Players featured in the albumBelow is the list of Brazil players who received a sticker in this edition, according to Estadão.Goalkeepers: Alisson and BentoDefenders: Marquinhos, Éder Militão, Gabriel Magalhães, Wesley and DaniloMidfielders: Bruno Guimarães, Lucas Paquetá and CasemiroForwards: Vinícius Júnior, Rodrygo, Luiz Henrique, João Pedro, Matheus Cunha, Gabriel Martinelli, Raphinha and EstêvãoRecord size and new pricesReflecting the World Cup’s new format, which will feature 48 national teams for the first time, the 2026 album will be the biggest in history.AdvertisementThe collection will have a total of 980 stickers, a significant jump from the 670 stickers in the 2022 edition.The publisher kept the same pricing pattern as in its latest general releases, but the final cost for collectors has increased compared with the last World Cup.Check out the official prices for the Brazilian market:Sticker pack: R$ 7.00 (with 7 stickers). For comparison, in 2022 the pack cost R$ 4.00 and included 5 stickers.Standard album (paperback): R$ 24.90Hardcover album: Up to R$ 79.90Special box: R$ 359.90 (includes the album and 40 packs)This article was translated into English by Artificial Intelligence. FIFA is dropping more tickets Wednesday originally appeared on NBC Sports Bay AreaNew tickets for all 104 matches of the 2026 FIFA World Cup will drop on Wednesday at 8 a.m. PT, FIFA announced Tuesday.AdvertisementThe matches will be played across Mexico, Canada and the United States from June 11 to July 19.It was not immediately clear how many tickets would be made available or how much they would cost.The new ticket inventory release to the general public comes with exactly 50 days before the tournament begins. According to FIFA, tickets will be available for several categories, including the front-row seat category, depending on the match.This drop is part of the ongoing “last-minute sales phase” that runs until the end of the tournament. FIFA said in a release that additional tickets will be released on a first-come, first-served basis.AdvertisementIn the release, FIFA reminded fans that their official website is the preferred source for World Cup tickets, and fans should check that site regularly for additional tickets that are made available on an ongoing basis. Additionally, the official resale/exchange marketplace is also available there for eligible ticket holders.FIFA has been scrutinized throughout the ticketing process, with outrage over transit prices in New Jersey, more expensive ticket packages and glitches in the systems.Powered byScan finds serious injury, and Brazil striker could miss World CupEstêvão’s participation in the World Cup with the Brazilian national team is at serious risk due to a hamstring injury suffered during Chelsea’s defeat to Manchester United last Saturday.According to The Athletic, the 18-year-old forward suffered a grade-four injury, making his presence at the World Cup highly unlikely, since the tournament is set to begin on June 11, and Brazil’s opener against Morocco takes place two days later.AdvertisementThe Athletic had already reported on April 18 that Estêvão would undergo imaging tests to assess the severity of the issue.According to Wednesday’s (22) report, by Mario Cortegana, Sebastian Stafford-Bloor and Liam Twomey, the MRI was carried out on Monday afternoon (20), and there was already a pessimistic mood behind the scenes at Chelsea even before the result came back.The injury happened just 16 minutes into the match at Stamford Bridge, in the 1-0 loss to Manchester United.The youngster left the pitch limping and, as manager Liam Rosenior confirmed after the match, was in tears in the dressing room.📸 GLYN KIRK - AFP or licensorsAdvertisementThe incident could bring Estêvão’s debut season at the English club to an early end.Signed from Palmeiras in May 2024, the attacking midfielder joined the squad in the middle of last year.In his first season in Europe, he posted strong numbers:Matches: 36Goals: 8 (including 3 in 7 Champions League matches)Assists: 4Importance to the Brazilian national teamEstêvão quickly established himself as a regular presence in Carlo Ancelotti’s Brazil side.The youngster has been called up 11 times to the senior team and comes into this stretch with four goals in his last four matches for the national team.At the World Cup, Brazil are in Group B, where they will face Morocco, Haiti and Scotland.AdvertisementChelsea, meanwhile, are going through a difficult spell: after losing 3-0 to Brighton on Tuesday, the team has only four Premier League matches remaining, along with an FA Cup semi-final against Leeds United next Sunday.This article was translated into English by Artificial Intelligence. You can read the original version in 🇧🇷 here.Story byFBL-LEGENDS-EXHIBITION-MEX-BRA - AFPEl trío emblemático vuelve a sus mejores tiemposA los 15 minutos, una jugada retro llevó la ventaja. Ronaldinho, de ‘10’, dejó atrás a Gerardo Torrado con un recorte y lanzó un pase preciso a Adriano.Advertisement«L'Imperatore» no defraudó: ante la salida del portero, elevó el balón con precisión y lo colocó en el fondo de la red. Un instante de pura técnica que calló momentáneamente a la afición local antes de que estallara en aplausos para los íconos brasileños.Mira el vídeoKaká amplía la ventaja con una jugada individualLa calidad individual de Brasil volvió a brillar cuando Kaká, exjugador del AC Milan y del Real Madrid, recibió el balón en la banda izquierda. Con su elegancia habitual, el ganador del Balón de Oro se deshizo de dos defensas y lanzó un disparo raso que entró por la esquina inferior.AdvertisementTras marcar, imitó un lanzamiento de baloncesto en homenaje a la leyenda brasileña Oscar Schmidt, “Mão Santa”. El gesto reforzó el ambiente festivo antes de la reacción mexicana.Las leyendas de México protagonizan una remontadaLuis Hernández devolvió al equipo local al partido al aprovechar un descuido defensivo y batir a Julio César, encendiendo al público y transformando la exhibición en un duelo reñido. Luego, Oribe Peralta —pesadilla recurrente de Brasil— encabezó la remontada.El atacante, famoso por su doblete en la final olímpica de 2012, igualó el marcador con un firme cabezazo al final del primer tiempo y, en la segunda parte, levantó el balón sobre el portero suplente Heurelho Gomes para sellar el 3-2.AdvertisementStory byThe Mexico national team will be led by a familiar face heading into the 2030 World Cup, FMF sporting director Duilio Davino confirmed this week, and there could be other Mexico legends coming alongside him.Davino confirmed the long-standing plans for Rafa Marquez to become the new boss of El Tri, leading Mexico as it begins its push toward the 2030 World Cup.AdvertisementMarquez is a legend of the Mexico national team, having played in five consecutive World Cups, and one of its most successful players ever at the club level. Marquez won the UEFA Champions League twice with Barcelona and also collected four La Liga titles with the Blaugrana. He also won league titles in France and Mexico."Yes, his contract is signed," Davino told Fox Sports this week. "His coaching staff is practically 80% complete."1 / 40Who qualified for 2026 World Cup? See every country in the tournamentSpain – 17th appearance2 / 40Who qualified for 2026 World Cup? See every country in the tournamentBrazil – 23rd appearance40 / 40Who qualified for 2026 World Cup? See every country in the tournamentHaiti – second appearanceThat coaching staff may include another Mexico legend. Former Mexico midfielder Andres Guardado, who like Marquez developed in the Atlas youth setup in Guadalajara, is coaching youth players at Real Betis but may be wooed to the national team setup."Andres is an option," Davino said. "At the end of the day, I’d like for me not to say, for him to say, but Andres is a very good option."AdvertisementWho will replace Javier Aguirre as Mexico national team coach?Marquez left his post as manager of Barcelona B to join current Mexico manager Javier Aguirre as his assistant and successor.But Marquez's success with Barcelona's second team and his name recognition in world soccer had some Mexico fans concerned that the succession plan may be derailed by a club making Marquez an offer he couldn't refuse. Now, it seems Marquez is still on course to live out his dream of leading his country, which he represented 147 times on the international stage and helped to the 1999 FIFA Confederations Cup plus a pair of Concacaf Gold Cup crowns.Davino feels the contrast between Marquez's charisma away from the field with the intensity he brings on it will make him a successful manager for Mexico heading into the 2030 World Cup.Advertisement"Rafa, off the field, is a personality," Davino said. "As a player on the field? Well, how he is today as an assistant and a coach is how he was as a player. He transforms in the locker room, on the training ground, on the field, then he gets out of the shower and he’s the Rafa he always is."Davino, himself a former Mexico defender who represented Mexico 84 times, appointed Aguirre with Marquez on the staff in the summer of 2024 after Jaime Lozano failed to lead El Tri out of the Copa América group stage.It was the third time Aguirre took charge of the national team, and the 67-year-old is widely expected to retire from the sport after this summer's World Cup.Mexico kicks off its World Cup campaign June 12 against South Africa at the Estadio Azteca in Mexico City before playing Korea and the Czech Republic.This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: Mexico national team legend Rafa Marquez set to take over El Tri
